newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Postbank, post office dispute said resolved.
newsitem.headline: German Postbank, post office dispute said resolved.

text.p: German postal minister Wolfgang Boetsch is expected to announce on Monday that Postbank AG and the post office have resolved a long-running dispute about the annual payment the bank should make for using post office counters.
Sources close to the talks said the state-owned companies, both earmarked for privatisation, had reached a deal just hours before an ultimatum set by Boetsch expired on October 31.
But details were not available and the companies declined official comment.
Boetsch, who is on a tour of Asian countries with Chancellor Helmut Kohl and a host of business leaders, is expected to reveal details on Monday after his return.
The post office demanded that Postbank pay 1.49 billion marks for the use of post office counters in 1997 while the bank offered just under one billion.
Boetsch had told the two sides to come up with a deal by the end of October or accept a compromise payment of 1.1 billion marks.
The post office has warned that payment of such a low sum would lead to the closure of thousands of post offices in the years to come.
Meanwhile, Postbank AG looks set to name a chief executive from the private sector to replace sixty-six-year-old Guenter Schneider, banking sources said.
Sixty-six year-old Schneider's contract expires at the end of 1996 but is likely to be extended for a further six months until a suitable successor is found, the sources said.
The Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper on Friday named Paul Wieandt, chief executive of BfG Bank AG, as Schneider's likely successor. Wieandt, 60, declined to comment.
BfG belongs to France's state-owned Credit Lyonnais.

Banking sources said it would make sense to appoint Wieandt, a former chief executive of state-owned regional bank Landesbank Rheinland-Pfalz, since he was experienced in restructuring and in dealing with politicians.
That experience could be useful in the difficult phase of Postbank's privatisation, the sources said.
The government plans to sell 75 percent of Postbank this year but the opposition Social Democrats said earlier this month that the sale was unlikely to be completed this year.
